study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial
exposure: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
outcome: type of neonatal feeding during hospital stay
cohort: 2,329 women with a singleton pregnancy who delivered at 34(0/7) to 36(6/7) weeks
finding: Several maternal and neonatal characteristics were associated with an increased risk of formula feeding in late preterm neonates, including smoking, cesarean delivery, and admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of formula feeding in late preterm neonates.
